8aaqxt:367: AI coding tools have evolved to the point where they are not just autocompleting a few lines of code. Tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex are gradually becoming true "partners" that can participate in the development process. But in real projects, one issue becomes increasingly obvious: ** AI isn't incapable of writing code—it's often unable to see the whole codebase. ** It may understand the current file, yet not know where else a function is called; it may complete a refactoring, but miss a cross-module dependency; sometimes it only changes an inconspicuous return value, and ends up affecting the entire downstream business flow. GitNexus aims to solve exactly this problem. It first organizes the codebase into a "knowledge graph," precomputing dependency relationships, call chains, functional clustering, and execution flows, then exposes them to AI Agents through MCP, CLI, Web UI, and more. In other words, GitNexus doesn't make the model "better at guessing"—it enables the model to truly understand your codebase before it starts changing code.
